chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one who is given a specific number of lashes (for false testimony), if he repents, is his testimony accepted? He said: 'If he repents, and his repentance is that he returns to what he said and calls himself a liar in the presence of the Imam and in the presence of the Muslims, then when he does so, it is upon the Imam to accept his testimony after that.'

key_terms.الْمَحْدُود: The one who has received the prescribed punishment (lashes) for false testimony

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for accepting the testimony of someone who gave false testimony and was lashed?
ai.summary: In the context of *tahdīth al-shuhūd* (validating witnesses), this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that mere internal repentance is insufficient; the individual must publicly retract their false statement (*rujūʿ*) and declare their previous testimony invalid before the Imam and the community. This public declaration ensures the restoration of their social credibility (*ʿadālah*), thereby obligating the Imam to accept their testimony anew, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the procedural integrity of legal testimony.
